posts.cooked:
What we Know

 

Contents
  • 5 heroes - Harpy, Akash, La Comodora, Lifeline, Luminary
  • 4 Villain decks - Oblivean, Scions, Aeonmen, and missions decks. Shield cards too
  • Comic Book
  • Two Environments
Extras
  • 27 hero variant cards
  • 6 additional heroes - Stunman, Benchmark, The Void Guard

 

Other Misc Info
  • The Void Guard heroes character cards are not intended to be able to be used when using the Sentinels deck. - Art Feed
  • The Void Guard will have special instructions included with it explaining how it interacts with the Sentinels deck. - Art Feed
  • One or more of the new (ex villain) heroes will have cards with previously villain exclusive keywords i.e. fowl, primieval limb, device - reddit ama
  • It's possible that Citizen Dawn is represented somehow within Oblivean - reddit ama
  • Luminary Info from Twitter Teaser - Lumniary - 27HP

    Innate Power: "Devise" - Power: Discard the top two cards of your deck. Move any Devices discarded this way into play. [Interesting that it says devices, not equipment]

    The nemesis icon on Luminary's card seems to be OblivAeon (The icon matches Obv's chestplate and the fuzzy filename text corroborates this)

    From the text entry box on one the other screen in the picture, you can also see:

    Lumniary's Incap Abilities: One player may play a card / One player may discard 2 cards. If they do, they may draw 2 cards. / Destroy 1 hero ongoing card. If you so, destroy up to 2 ongoing cards. [From text entry screen]

    Variant Luminary's Innate Power: "Empowered Attack" - Power: Luminary deals 1 target X lighning damage, where X = the number of Devices in play plus 1. [From text entry screen]

  • The Harpy seems to involve some sort of flippable tokens. Dark Watch Harpy has 27 HP.

  • It appears Harpy and Luminary have the same nemesis icon, but they could be placeholder icons to avoid revealing secrets.

 

 

This topic is intended to help keep known info from the Reddit Ama, art feeds and such into one place. I probably missed plenty of things, so feel free to comment and I'll update it.

posts.name: Voob Gooblin
posts.cooked:
Sooooo how do people feel about potentially having up to 11 character cards (& 11 variants) with the same nemesis icon?

Personally, I feel a bit wary of that prospect, as

1) It seems silly and arbitrary that a bunch of unrelated heros could all do nemesis damage to each other (I've always used the "from different decks" house rule for Ennead, Sentinels, & Chairman/Operative silliness, but now that's not quite enough to cover it).

2) Several heros will have an icon design that has nothing to do with the hero, but reference OblivAeon instead, which feels off, and kind of boring.

3) I was hoping the new heros would find nemeses in specific Scion cards, rather than just OblivAeon itself, and now that seems unlikely.

Maybe there's more to this than it seems? I hope there is more to this than it seems.

posts.name: aawood
posts.cooked:
Voob Gooblin:

It seems silly and arbitrary that a bunch of unrelated heros could all do nemesis damage to each other (I've always used the "from different decks" house rule for Ennead, Sentinels, & Chairman/Operative silliness, but now that's not quite enough to cover it)

I don't have much to say on the rest, but for this; most of the new Heroes (as in the game mechanic term to refer to playable decks) are not heroes (as in people who want to do good and help), they're villains who, thematically, are choosing to co-operate only because of this huge threat. It makes a lot of sense to me that they wouldn't be very good team players. Whether by ego, lack of experience working with others, or just because they feel collateral damage is nothing if they can stop this huge threat, they're bound to get in each other's way and not caring about hurting the others.

Meanwhile, the existing heroes are both used to working in a team, and aware that these characters, while the enemy of their enemy, aren't actually their friends. As such, they're doing a better job of keeping out of the way and letting the villains heroes do their thing, which is why they're not taking any more damage from them than the usual accidentaly friendly fire that happens from time to time.

posts.name: Voob Gooblin
posts.cooked:
I don't really have a problem with the new villains-turned-heroes sharing a single nemesis in OblivAeon. That makes sense, narratively. I take issue with the way this would work mechanically, and with the seeming lack of creativity in handling this mechanic (and graphics) for the final hero decks (although I admit this is going off very little information, and there may be more to it than we know).

Theoretically, you could build the same narrative thread by having unique icons for each new hero and just putting each of those icons on OblivAeon's cards (e.g. Iron Legacy), allowing each hero character card to have a unique, character-relevant icon and preventing any arbitrary friendly-fire shenanigans in future games (the apologetics for why this makes sense just don't work for me). I guess the only downside is the amount of real estate that would be taken up on OblivAeon's cards.

Either way, this still just feels a bit boring to me—I'd rather that they keep the nemeses they had in current heroes, or find new nemeses in Scions, with whom they either have past relationships or newly developed emnity; either would be more interesting to me, narratively and mechanically.

I could never buy into the justification for the Ennead/Sentinels nemesis damage silliness, since there are so many allies and teams that don't do extra damage to each other—and now we have several heros who are completely unrelated (other than the fact that they used to be villains) potentially doing extra damage to each other because of a mechanical fluke. I get that it's just a flawed minor mechanic, but I do feel it could be utilized more creatively.

Anyway I'll stop nattering on about this now.
